w: The Bay Area's dim sum benchmark for Cantonese banquet cooking; the har gow come with near-translucent skins over sweet whole shrimp, alongside flaky baked BBQ-pork buns and whole roast duck.
sources: theinfatuation.com/san-francisco/reviews/koi-palace - 'the dim sum gold standard in the Bay Area' (review of the Koi Palace flagship; Milpitas is the South Bay outpost)
Eater SF feature 'How Dim Sum Legend Koi Palace Preserves the Legacy of Cantonese Banquet Culture'

w: One of the dwindling handful of South Bay rooms still doing dim sum cart service; carts roll out har gow bursting with juicy shrimp plus super-crispy sesame balls with sweet red-bean paste.
sources: theinfatuation.com/san-francisco/reviews/fu-lam-mum - 'great dim sum and one of the dwindling handful still doing cart service'

address: 10745 S De Anza Blvd, Cupertino, CA 95014
w: The first Bay Area shop to specialize in Gansu-province Lanzhou noodles; choose your noodle cut for a clear, 10-hour spiced beef broth, or get the flat noodles with the ten-hour Sichuan-braised beef stew.
sources: guide.michelin.com — Ox 9 Lanzhou is Michelin-recommended (also featured Michelin Cover Story 2018)

address: 3561 El Camino Real #10, Santa Clara, CA 95051
w: A longtime anchor of Santa Clara's El Camino Koreatown and a repeat Michelin Guide selection; the tabletop galbi (marinated beef short ribs) and stone-pot stews arrive with a generous banchan spread.
sources: MICHELIN Guide selected restaurant, Santa Clara (Korean); multi-year California Guide listing

w: The Tokyo chain's first U.S. shop, famous for long nightly waits; the Original King is a silky 24-hour tonkotsu you customize by richness, garlic and a 1-to-10 spice scale.
sources: Japan's Ramen Nagi arrives to elevate Palo Alto's noodle game — https://www.paloaltoonline.com/uncategorized/2018/06/19/japans-ramen-nagi-arrives-to-elevate-palo-altos-noodle-game/
Bowls of Bliss at Ramen Nagi — https://www.metrosiliconvalley.com/bowls-of-bliss-at-ramen-nagi/

w: A bare-bones mainstay in historic San Jose Japantown for comforting teishoku; go for the tangy chicken teriyaki, breaded katsu cutlets and savory udon.
